## Separate RW and TO models {#rd02-separate-species-review}

Each species uses `ba_ha ~ treat + (1 | site/treat)`: site and nested macro-plot
intercepts, zero-inflated Gamma responses, and species-specific zero and
dispersion intercepts. The plot-level random effect is omitted.

The focused comparison shows the main difference: separate fitting increases
RW's GS mean and uncertainty, while TO changes less. Separate-model GS means
are `r rd02_mean_ci("separate_site_macro_pair", "rw", "gs")` for RW and
`r rd02_mean_ci("separate_site_macro_pair", "to", "gs")` m² ha⁻¹ for TO
(mean and 95% CI).

See @fig-rd02-separate-species-comparison beside its generating code above.

## Summary and model decision {#rd02-review-recommendation}

**Selected approach.** Fit redwood, tanoak, Douglas-fir, and other species
separately with treatment as a fixed effect and site and nested macro-plot
random intercepts. This choice prioritizes biological interpretation and
species-specific variance estimation. The RW/TO figure is in the Results;
all-category values are in the supplement. The joint-model comparisons remain
as sensitivity evidence.

All four selected fits converge with positive-definite Hessians and no flags
in the overall residual checks. Macro-plot variances approach zero; site
variation differs substantially among categories, with Douglas-fir also near
zero. Means include zeros and integrate over both random effects. Four sites
still limit variance precision; interval stability remains a useful bootstrap
check before final inferential claims.
